correctness.rationale: The frozen eight-file Git tree matches the assigned source-tree identity. For μ,κ>0, p=1+2μy−κy² has distinct zeros y_± and H=(x²+y²)/p is constant on p≠0 by direct differentiation; H=E gives x²+(1+κE)y²−2μEy−E=0. Sign constraints split the two isolated critical equilibria, two regular elliptical annuli, two invariant horizontal lines, one invariant parabola and the remaining hyperbolic branches. The exact ellipse-time integral yields T0=2π and T1=2πμ/√(μ²+κ). On y=y_±, Riccati integration gives F_±=π(1±μ/√q). On y=−(1+κx²)/(2μ), differentiation gives dot{x}=((1+κx²)^2+4μ²x²)/(4μ)>0 and the full positive quartic integral yields Fp=2πμ/√q. The quartic leading term proves x blow-up exponent 1/3 and coefficient (4μ/(3κ²))^(1/3). Riccati lines give exponent 1 and |x||Δt|→1/√q; for h>1/κ the hyperbolic asymptotes x/y→±√(κh−1) and dot{y}∼−κxy² give finite two-sided escape and Δt·y²→[2κ√(κh−1)]^-1. These algebraic and analytic steps prove the universal parameter quantifiers; the supplied verify.py checks only core symbolic identities, not the integral/exhaustion proof. Independent SymPy differentiation/parabolic tangency and three numerical quadratures were corroborative, not the universal proof.
residual_risks: The analytic proof uses the standard contour integral ∫(d+Bsinφ)^(-1)dφ and positive biquadratic integral; both are stated with hypotheses and reduce to elementary exact formulas.
Only μ>0, κ>0 and real maximal classical solutions are proved; singular parameter axes, complex time and perturbations are excluded.
No formal Lean proof or expert attestation exists; symbolic and numerical checks do not substitute for the analytic geometry.
